synthesis:draft.headline: SA1 five-minute RRP peaked at 4981.0 $/MWh (2026-07-31 02:05 ACST (UTC+0930)).
summary: Peak five-minute RRP in SA1 was 4981.0 $/MWh at 2026-07-31 02:05 ACST (UTC+0930).
Two hundred fourteen five-minute intervals met the analysis threshold of 300.0 $/MWh.
Dispatch TOTALDEMAND at the five-minute peak interval end was 1472.82 MW, with net interchange -82.59 MW (net flow into SA1 / import).
Operational demand for the half-hour ending 2026-07-31 02:30 ACST (UTC+0930) was 1466.0 MW; the window maximum operational demand was 2173.0 MW at 2026-07-30 19:00 ACST (UTC+0930).

numeric_claims.text: Peak five-minute RRP in SA1 was 4981.0 $/MWh
Number of five-minute intervals meeting the analysis threshold: 214
Analysis threshold used by the project: 300.0 $/MWh
Dispatch TOTALDEMAND at the five-minute peak interval end was 1472.82 MW
Net interchange at the peak interval was -82.59 MW
Operational demand for the half-hour ending 2026-07-31 02:30 ACST was 1466.0 MW
Window maximum operational demand was 2173.0 MW

possible_explanations.statement: Lower regional wind generation might have contributed to reduced supply around the event; the Adelaide-point WS50M wind speed context and several large unit output reductions are relevant (see evidence ev1008, ev1019 and unit-change evidence ev0940, ev0943, ev0946, ev0949).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Obtain an aggregate regional SNSG/non-scheduled wind generation time series at five-minute resolution for SA1 through the window, and retrieve unit technology metadata for the listed duids to verify which changes are wind; compare aggregate wind output at the peak interval to its typical level.

possible_explanations.statement: Network or interconnector limitations might have amplified the price outcome; see the Belalie-Davenport line outage notice [c2] and the net interchange value ev0438.
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Retrieve interconnector capability timelines, constraint binding logs and constraint sets invoked around the peak interval to see whether transfer limits or constraint binding reduced import capability.

possible_explanations.statement: Demand and local unit availability changes might have been relevant, given the half-hour operational demand and observed unit output changes (evidence ev0913 and ev0940–ev0949).
possible_explanations.what_would_test_it: Review unit availability, rebids and offers for scheduled and semi-scheduled units in the half-hour ending 2026-07-31 02:30 ACST (2026-07-30T17:00:00Z) and check unit outage records to determine supply-side availability changes.

uncertainties: The weather context is a model-derived hourly series at one point (Adelaide) and may not represent region-wide wind conditions (evidence ev1008, ev1019).

The generation-change tool reports large unit output changes but does not label unit technology in the returned fields; which changed units are wind is not present in those evidence items (e.g. ev0940, ev0943, ev0946, ev0949).
Constraint binding, interconnector capability timelines and unit offer/rebid histories were not returned and are required to distinguish supply limitation vs network/constraint effects.
missing_evidence: Aggregate regional SNSG/non-scheduled wind generation time series for SA1 at five-minute resolution through the window (to show total wind output at the peak interval).
Unit metadata mapping duids to technology (wind/thermal) for the duids in the generation-change list (e.g. TORRB3, TORRB2, BARKIPS1, QPS5).
Constraint binding logs and interconnector capability timelines around the peak interval.
Unit availability and rebid/offer histories for scheduled and semi-scheduled units covering the half-hour ending 2026-07-31 02:30 ACST (2026-07-30T17:00:00Z).
